description.shortText: An offshore wind turbine mounted on a floating structure that generates electricity in water depths where fixed-foundation turbines are not feasible. Floating wind turbines, when stabilized by anchors and a buoyant substructure, can generate more electricity than current wind propellers.

attachments.name: IBM Supercomputers Help Vestas Squeeze the Most Out of Wind Farms
attachments.description: Supercomputers can help us figure out where are the best spots for wind farms. This kind of optimization can increase clean energy production per installed turbine.

attachments.name: Offshore Wind Outlook 2019
attachments.description: Offshore wind is a rapidly maturing renewable energy technology that is poised to play an important role in future energy systems. In 2018, offshore wind provided a tiny fraction of global electricity supply, but it is set to expand strongly in the coming decades into a $1 trillion business. Turbines are growing in size and in terms of the power capacity they can provide, which in turn is delivering major performance and cost improvements for offshore wind farms.

attachments.name: How does a floating wind turbine stand up?
attachments.description: It is not just utility companies racing to respond to the rise of renewable energy. Oil and gas giant Statoil is building on four decades of offshore experience to erect its first floating wind farm.

attachments.name: How can we make floating wind farms cost-effective?
attachments.description: Offshore wind is a great generator of renewable energy, but it is not very cost-effective. Developing new technologies using AI could change this.
